corrected_content.problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(-1,1)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $\mathbf{T},$ given by

$$
\mathbf{T}:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}⟶\begin{bmatrix}v{e}^{u} \\ u{e}^{v}\end{bmatrix}?
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))≈|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\cdot \underbrace{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{\delta A}
$$

 

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =\begin{vmatrix}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}v{e}^{u} & {e}^{u} \\ {e}^{v} & u{e}^{v}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =v{e}^{u}\cdot u{e}^{v}-{e}^{v}\cdot {e}^{u} \\  & =uv{e}^{u+v}-{e}^{u+v} \\  & =(uv-1){e}^{u+v} \\ {\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(-1,1)} & =(uv-1){e}^{u+v}\,{|}_{u=-1\,v=1} \\  & =(-1\cdot 1-1){e}^{-1+1} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & ≈|-2|\cdot \delta A \\  & =2\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$
